QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the energy per mole of photon of electromagnetic radiation having wavelength $700$ nm ($h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ Js, $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s)

Solution.S:
Energy of one photon is given by $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$.

Given: $\lambda = 700 \times 10^{-9}$ m, $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ Js, $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s.

$$E = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{700 \times 10^{-9}} = 2.84 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$$

Energy per mole of photons = $E \times N_A$.

$$= 2.84 \times 10^{-19} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}$$
$$= 1.71 \times 10^5 \text{ J/mol}$$

Thus, the correct option is A: $1.71 \times 10^5$ J.
